focus: RQ-2 and RQ-3: seven runtime loaders, Hermes copy contents, and runtime versus parser context
noveltyJustification: This iteration maps each runtime packaging path and distinguishes skill instructions loaded by the agent from structures parsed by tools.
answeredQuestions: RQ-2: How do Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Cursor, Pi, Devin and Hermes load a skill, and do they load sibling files automatically? What does the Hermes copy step include?
RQ-3: Which machine-router facts does an agent need in context at runtime, which facts only scripts need, and what pointer must remain in SKILL.md?
ruledOut: Assuming that a sibling ROUTER.md is automatically added to model context merely because it sits beside SKILL.md.
edgeCase: repo-specific skill discovery differs from native runtime discovery

label: Workspace delivery differs by runtime: Claude, OpenCode, Pi, and Devin expose the canonical skills tree through directory symlinks; Hermes builds standalone SKILL.md copies; Codex has no .codex/skills tree; Cursor has no .cursor/skills tree but current Cursor docs also discover .claude/skills, which this checkout links to .skilled/skills. The local Cursor manifest records only its own skills location, so refresh that description alongside the migration.

The skill runtimes use progressive loading: they advertise metadata or a description, then load SKILL.md when selected; supporting-file contents are read only when the instructions call for them. OpenCode states this explicitly, while Claude, Pi, Cursor, and Codex document the same on-demand pattern. A sibling ROUTER.md therefore needs an explicit path and read instruction in SKILL.md; directory presence alone does not put its text in the model context.

This checkout does not provision a Codex-native skills directory: its Codex sync manifest says there is no .codex/skills, and the root AGENTS.md routes through the skill-advisor hook or explicit advisor CLI. OpenAI documents repo-local Codex skills under .agents/skills, but that root is not present in this checkout; treat Codex loading here as explicit canonical-path routing, not automatic project skill discovery.

The Hermes sync walks only files named SKILL.md, writes one generated markdown file per skill, and rewrites relative Markdown links to point back to the canonical skill directory. It deliberately excludes references, scripts, assets, and other sibling files, so a relocated ROUTER.md will not be in the Hermes preload copy; the generator must either add that one sidecar or rewrite the pointer to its canonical .skilled path.

Agents still need the intent-selection rule, exact route destinations, load levels, and low-confidence or ambiguity fallback when they choose skill resources; the canonical smart-router template explicitly describes discovery, path guards, conditional loads, a runtime key, and fallback as router behavior. Literal delimiters and assignment shapes are also consumed by replay, validation, measurement, and package tooling, but those parsers should read the sidecar directly instead of requiring the script syntax to remain inside SKILL.md.

Keep a short pointer in SKILL.md that names sibling ROUTER.md, says to read it before selecting or loading skill-local resources, and resolves it from the skill directory. This preserves progressive loading while keeping the route available on demand. The pointer policy conflicts with the current authoring template statement that mode packets never carry ROUTER.md, so the authoring template, creation workflows, parser checks, and tests must be revised together before migration.
